answer: One workable design: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because delta only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, oasis is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
